title: 2px line at top of screen when using WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN and Compatibility in Windows
body:
### Tested versions

 - Reproducible in 4.6-beta2 and later
 - Not reproducible in earlier versions of 4.6 nor 4.5.
 - Not relevant to test in versions earlier than 4.5 as WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN worked differently.

### System information

Godot v4.6.3.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 960 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13400F (16 threads) - 15.85 GiB memory

### Issue description

When using WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN in the Compatibility renderer there is a 2px wide line (coloured either black or the BG Color) at the top of the screen in Windows. This appears both when playing the game from the editor and in exported executables.

In my testing it has not appeared when using Forward+ or the Mobile renderers, only Compatibility.

I have tested this on various systems and it does not seem to affect either Linux or Mac exports, only Windows.

I have tested it on a few Windows (10 & 11) systems both desktop and laptop and the issue is present in all I have tested except for one, a laptop with integrated Intel HD Graphics 620, which I'm assuming is because it uses ANGLE. All the other test systems had discrete Nvidia cards. It was also present when running through Proton on Linux.

I think I've pinpointed the cause of the regression to [110375](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/110375) as I created a custom build of 4.6.3 with this PR reverted and the problem went away. I'm unclear why this PR would have only created the issue for the Compatibility renderer though - nothing struck me as obviously incorrect from a very naive reading of the code changes. I don't know whether you could shed any light on this @bruvzg?

### Steps to reproduce

View any project made in 4.6-beta2 and later that uses the Compability renderer in WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN on (most?) Windows systems and note the 2px line at the top of the screen. My MRP shows this clearly by using a black ColorRect with the BG Color set to red.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[compat_2pxline.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30719127/compat_2pxline.zip)
